description: Dynamics description uses incorrect rotational kinematics by setting Euler angle derivatives equal to body angular rates (`Euler angle derivative = current angular velocity`). For ZYX Euler angles, `[φ̇, θ̇, ψ̇]` is not equal to `[p, q, r]` except under small-angle/approximate assumptions; using this as “nonlinear equations of motion” will yield wrong attitude evolution.

locations.section: Dynamics (Equations of Motion) → Implementation Logic → 3. Euler angle derivative

description: Rotational dynamics are described as `Angular velocity derivative = I⁻¹ M` while calling the model “nonlinear equations of motion”. This omits the standard rigid-body coupling term `ω × (I ω)` (i.e., `I ω̇ = M − ω×(Iω)`), which is a concrete modeling error for a supposedly nonlinear quadrotor simulator.

description: Physical acceleration-limit guidance hardcodes specific numeric limits (e.g., 6.962, −9.429, 13.602 m/s²) and frames them as the required bounds. The task explicitly requires enforcing the limits from `system_params.yaml` keys (`accel_limit_up`, `accel_limit_down`, `accel_limit_horiz`). Hardcoding derived constants can directly violate the task’s stated source of truth.

Example output-writing code states “Save tuning results (same content for every command)”, which contradicts the task requirement to tune PID parameters per command and save the best PID gains found for that command in each command’s results folder.
